_comment: A settled country's laws and code: for each law, one option is in force. default: the option countries start with unless their country file says otherwise. requires: a condition (see data/countries/EGY.json flags) the country must meet to adopt the option, described by requires_text. modifiers change the country's numbers: tax (share more), noncitizen_tax (share more from non-citizens), noncitizen_manpower (share of their manpower raised; citizens give it all), uprising (share more likely), years_to_core (years added), tribe_relations (added to tribes' opinion), alliance_chance (added), building_cost (share more), mercenary_pay (share more), change_cost (share more to change laws). effects are ongoing: assimilation (units per core province a year turning to the ruler's culture), conversion (to the ruler's religion), succession (how the next ruler is chosen), citizens (who is a citizen).

laws.name: Succession
laws.description: Who takes the throne when the ruler dies.

options.name: Primogeniture
options.description: The ruler's eldest son inherits. The dynasty goes on; the heir may be young.

options.name: Agnatic seniority
options.description: The ruler's eldest brother inherits: older, seasoned rulers, and the dynasty goes on.

options.name: Elective council
options.description: The great men of the realm choose the ablest among them. A new dynasty may rise.

options.name: Divine selection
options.description: The priests read the will of the gods and name the next ruler. Temples grow powerful.

laws.name: Citizenship
laws.description: Who is a citizen: citizens pay the full tax and serve in the army.

options.name: Only the ruling people
options.description: Only those of the ruler's culture are citizens.

options.name: Kindred peoples
options.description: Those who speak a language of the ruler's language family are citizens too.

options.name: All settled subjects
options.description: Every settled subject is a citizen; tribesmen and nomads are not.

options.name: All subjects
options.description: Everyone under the ruler's protection is a citizen, settled or not.
options.requires_text: A realm of at least 40 provinces

laws.name: Treatment of non-citizens
laws.description: How those who are not citizens are treated.

options.name: Protected subjects
options.description: Non-citizens live under the ruler's protection: taxed lightly, they give some soldiers.

options.name: Tributaries
options.description: Non-citizens pay tribute, and give few soldiers.

options.name: Bonded labour
options.description: Non-citizens are bound to work the land and the quarries for the state: they pay much, fight not, and seethe.

laws.name: Other cultures
laws.description: How the state treats the cultures other than the ruler's.

options.name: Tolerance
options.description: Every people keeps its ways.

options.name: Assimilation
options.description: Other peoples are drawn into the ruler's culture: a unit a year in each core province.

options.name: Segregation
options.description: Other peoples are kept apart: less unrest among the ruling people, more among the rest, and new lands take longer to become ours.

laws.name: Religious law
laws.description: The place of the gods in the state.

options.name: Free worship
options.description: Every people worships its own gods; the state takes no side.

options.name: State cult
options.description: The ruler's gods are the state's gods; their temples collect offerings for the crown.

options.name: Enforced worship
options.description: All must worship the ruler's gods: other faiths convert, a unit a year in each core province.

options.name: Customary law
options.description: Each village judges by its old customs.

options.name: Codified law
options.description: The ruler's scribes write down the law and appoint judges: order, and a steadier hand in building.

options.name: Harsh code
options.description: Swift and brutal punishment keeps the provinces quiet, and frightens the tribes.

laws.name: Slavery
laws.description: Whether men may own other men.

options.name: Legal
options.description: Captives and debtors may be enslaved: cheap labour, but the tribes fear being taken.

options.name: Outlawed
options.description: No one may be owned. The tribes trust us more.
options.requires_text: Non-citizens must not be held in bonded labour

laws.name: The frontier
laws.description: How the tribes and nomads beyond our borders are dealt with.

options.name: Open frontier
options.description: Tribesmen come and go to trade: they think better of us.

options.name: Guarded frontier
options.description: Forts watch the desert roads: fewer raids and uprisings, cooler tribes.

options.name: Mercenary pacts
options.description: Tribal warriors are hired on standing terms: cheaper mercenaries.
